retention.stated: The server persists while the term is paid. The order page states no deletion schedule; the group page offers no refund term.

interface_detail: KVM guest with full root access, Linux templates or a custom ISO, managed through VirtFusion with VNC console and rescue mode.
tooling: Any SSH client; KVM means your own kernel, so WireGuard is loaded inside the guest without depending on the host.
chaining: A 1 GB KVM guest in Falkenstein with a /64 and 2.5 TB a month for USD 10.50 a year: the cheapest machine that can run its own kernel.

notes: The annual term is USD 10.50 against USD 17.25 for twelve monthly payments, so the annual prepay is the only way this machine is under the line. WireGuard should work here because KVM gives the guest its own kernel; that is a design property, not a measurement, and was not probed. | 2026-10-24: the entity is now established. HostBrr's own terms name PFWeb Solutions as the operator, and two Danish registry mirrors return a CVR number, status Aktiv, a sole proprietorship founded 21 April 2023 in Glostrup with www.hostbrr.com as its website. datacvr.virk.dk itself answered a Cloudflare bot challenge and proff.dk refused the request, so the primary register was not read. This is the beefiest machine in the sub-USD-1 band by RAM (1 GB) and the only one with a verifiable European registration that is definitely trading. The catch is the address family: no IPv4 at all, so a WireGuard peer must have working IPv6, and the vendor publishes no port policy because a routed /64 needs none.

extras.price_arithmetic: USD 10.50 a year / 12 = USD 0.875 a month, paid once. The monthly cycle on the same page is USD 1.4375, so annual prepay is the only way under the line. A VPS bills whether it runs or not, so the 24/7 and 10 h/day figures are the same.

network_out.ports: all, over IPv6 only; there is no IPv4 address and no NAT forwarding layer on this plan

extras.renewal_note: The order page sells three cycles for the same machine: 1 Month @ USD 1.4375, 3 Months @ USD 3.25, 1 Year @ USD 10.50. The annual rate of USD 0.875 a month is therefore a volume discount off a published monthly rate, and USD 1.4375 a month is the ceiling if the annual cycle is withdrawn.

extras.price_risk: 1.64x if the annual cycle stops being offered; the monthly rate is published, so the exposure is bounded
extras.udp: not stated as such, and none needs to be: the plan has a routed /64 and no port-forwarding layer, so a UDP listener needs only the guest firewall open. The vendor prints no port policy on the order page. Inferred from the architecture, not measured.
